user_query: create me a SQL query to find the top 10 best-selling products in the last 3 years, including their category and subcategory, total quantity sold, total revenue generated, average selling price, number of distinct customers who bought them, and the best sales territory for each product. Use the saleslt schema.
generated_sql:
SELECT TOP 10 pc.Name AS Category, ps.Name AS Subcategory, p.Name AS Product, SUM(sod.OrderQty) AS TotalQuantitySold, SUM(sod.LineTotal) AS TotalRevenueGenerated, p.ListPrice AS AverageSellingPrice, COUNT(DISTINCT soh.CustomerID) AS NumberOfDistinctCustomers, st.Name AS BestSalesTerritory
FROM saleslt.SalesOrderDetail sod
JOIN saleslt.Product p ON sod.ProductID = p.ProductID
JOIN saleslt.ProductCategory pc ON p.ProductCategoryID = pc.ProductCategoryID
JOIN saleslt.ProductSubcategory ps ON p.ProductSubcategoryID = ps.ProductSubcategoryID
JOIN saleslt.SalesOrderHeader soh ON sod.SalesOrderID = soh.SalesOrderID
JOIN saleslt.SalesTerritory st ON soh.TerritoryID = st.TerritoryID
WHERE soh.OrderDate >= DATEADD(year, -3, GETDATE())
GROUP BY pc.Name, ps.Name, p.Name, p.ListPrice, st.Name
ORDER BY TotalQuantitySold DESC
reasoning: The query was constructed by joining the necessary tables to gather information about product sales. The SalesOrderDetail table provides details on each product sold, while the Product, ProductCategory, and ProductSubcategory tables provide product information. The SalesOrderHeader table provides customer and order information, and the SalesTerritory table provides territory information. The query filters orders to only include those from the last 3 years and groups results by product category, subcategory, product name, and territory. The results are sorted in descending order by total quantity sold.
